content:
pagerduty-bot: PAGE -> Severity: P2. Streaming API latency SLO breach (p99 > 5s) for hosted/region-us-west-2. Alert: streaming_response_latency_p99 > 5s for 3m. Pager: https://pd.example/INC-7723987650 :rotating_light:

alex_k: oncall here, ack. seeing customer-facing errors?

jordan_s: looking at dashboards -> p95 from 220ms -> ~1.1s; p99 spiked to ~8s for streaming endpoints. Error rate (5xx) up from 0.1% -> 1.8% on the same timeframe. Streaming stalls flagged: 1) chunk backlog grows, 2) retransmit spikes.

maria_g: which customers impacted? any enterprise tenants? CX pinged?

lina_p: quick check: top-10 tenants by tokens show tenant-347 and tenant-903 with large streaming sessions starting ~10:12 UTC. Tenant-347 has high disk write IOPS on GPU host gpu-node-17.

mlinfra: prelim hypothesis: noisy neighbor on shared GPU pool causing blkio congestion -> streaming tail latency. I see cgroup throttling counters incrementing on gpu-node-17.

deploy-bot: recent deploys? no deploys to serving in last 30m. Canary stable.

alex_k: can someone dump iostat and cgroup stats from gpu-node-17? If a tenant is doing heavy logging or checkpointing it could saturate host IO.

jordan_s: running PromQL now:
```
# p99 latency for streaming by host
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_response_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, host))
```
host=\"gpu-node-17\": 8.1s, others ~0.12s.

mlinfra: grabbing blkio stats:
```
# on gpu-node-17
cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes
# sample: 8GB read, 12GB write in last 5m, write_ios: 180k
```

lina_p: also seeing kernel writeback spikes and dmesg showing slow nvme flush warnings around 10:13.

maria_g: customer impact: two enterprise customers (acme-corp, beta-app) reported degraded streaming quality and intermittent 5xx. I'm starting an incident banner and notifying account EMs.

alex_k: mitigation options: 1) throttle/limit noisy tenant, 2) evict runner(s) from gpu-node-17 and migrate, 3) change cgroup weights to favor serving lanes, 4) temporarily route new streaming sessions away from that host. Prefer lowest-risk quick action: set cgroup blkio weight for tenant cgroup and evict if not improving.

jordan_s: sequence to perform live mitigation (I have ssh to control plane):
1) identify pod(s) for tenant-347/903: `kubectl -n infer get pods -o wide | grep tenant-347`
2) cordon node: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17`
3) move short-lived inference pods: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (will respect PDBs)
4) if drain is slow, kill heavy worker processes: `pkill -f checkpoint_writer` on offending pod(s) (kill triggers restart onto other hosts)

mlinfra: adding lower-level cgroup tweak first to test: set blkio.weight for tenant cgroups to 200 (default 500) for the noisy pod's cgroup path. Command:
```
echo 200 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/<tenant-cgroup>/blkio.weight
```
This should throttle their IO without evicting.

alex_k: do it. Jordan, be ready to cordon/drain if no improvement in 60s.

mlinfra: applied blkio.weight=200 to tenant-347 cgroup at 10:19:27 UTC.

deploy-bot: alert suppression: muting streaming-high-latency alert for host=gpu-node-17 for 10m by user mlinfra.

jordan_s: watch metrics...

(30s pass)

jordan_s: latency p99 dropped from 8.1s -> 2.9s, p95 down to 520ms, error rate trending down. Not back to baseline yet.

maria_g: customer update: acme-corp now reports partial improvement but still seeing occasional stalls. Sending interim note saying we're mitigating and investigating root cause.

alex_k: good. Let's keep blkio throttle for 15m and plan migration of heavy jobs off node. Lina, can you identify if tenant-903 also contributing?

lina_p: tenant-903 is heavy read/write too but mostly checkpointing to local disk every 2m; we can temporarily disable checkpointing via runtime flag for that tenant: POST to admin API `/admin/tenants/903/flags` {"disable_checkpointing":true}. Permission required.

mlinfra: disabling checkpointing for tenant-903 now.

(quick success)

lina_p: checkpointing disabled at 10:21:40 UTC. IO write volume drops by ~60%.

jordan_s: metrics now: p99 1.1s, p95 260ms, errors back to ~0.15%. Looks near baseline.

alex_k: nice. Next steps: keep throttles for 10m, uncordon when migrations complete. We'll follow up with tenant owners to throttle at tenant-level and ask them to change checkpoint cadence.

maria_g: open support tickets for acme-corp + beta-app summarizing incident and mitigations. Also ask for post-incident call with their engineering leads.

mlinfra: logging notes: captured `iostat -x`, `dmesg`, and cgroup counters; saved to /var/log/incidents/7723987650/ on gpu-node-17.

jordan_s: I'm going to kick an automated host evacuation job for gpu-node-17 to move persistent heavy pods to other nodes during the maintenance window.

alex_k: escalation? Do we need paging to infra oncall or exec?

maria_g: not yet exec-level. We'll include SLO breach in postmortem and escalate to infra if this repeats within 7d.

deploy-bot: infra autoscaling not triggered due to reserved capacity rules. Consider temporary burst capacity for hot customers.

alex_k: handoff to next oncall in 30m: jordan_s will remain primary until 10:50 UTC, then handoff to lina_p. Document actions in incident tracker.

jordan_s: I've updated the incident doc: https://inc.example/7723987650 with timeline and mitigation steps. Leaving note: immediate cause = tenant checkpoint + heavy logging causing host nvme writeback + cgroup blkio throttling -> streaming stalls.

lina_p: taking over at 10:50 UTC. I'll keep the blkio weight reduced until migrations finish and then gradually restore. Follow-ups: 1) add static tenant IO limits, 2) detect host writeback spikes and auto-evict, 3) tenant-facing guidance on checkpoint cadence.

maria_g: assigning action items to SRE and Product: create runbook for GPU-host IO saturation and orchestrated eviction flow. Also reach out to tenant owners for mitigation steps.

alex_k: closing notes: immediate customer impact mitigated. P95/p99 back within acceptable window. We'll run full postmortem. :white_check_mark: 

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-7723987650 moved to status: acknowledged -> mitigated by user alex_k at 10:27:12 UTC.

jordan_s: final: leaving logs and commands used in the incident doc. Will open a follow-up to automate cgroup weight enforcement for heavy tenants.

lina_p: thanks team. Handoff complete.
